components.name: Alert
components.tagline: Inline, non-blocking message for status and feedback across four severities, with an optional floating (toast) treatment.

props.name: severity
props.description: Semantic state. Drives the colour and the default icon. Colours resolve from the token-built theme palette.

props.name: floating
props.description: Renders as a tinted, bordered, rounded surface with no default icon — for Alert used as a toast (e.g. inside `Snackbar`) rather than inline in the page.

props.name: title
props.description: Optional bold title rendered above the message.

props.name: children
props.description: The alert message body. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: onClose
props.description: When provided (and no `action`), renders a close button that fires on click. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: action
props.description: Element rendered after the message, justified to the end — e.g. a Button. Replaces the default close button. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the leading icon. Set to `false` to remove it. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: iconMapping
props.description: Override the per-severity icon. Defaults to the Neoflo Phosphor set.

examples.title: Severities
examples.description: The `severity` prop sets the colour and icon. All four resolve from the theme palette.
examples.code:
<Alert severity="error">Something went wrong.</Alert>
<Alert severity="warning">Your trial ends soon.</Alert>
<Alert severity="success">Changes saved.</Alert>
<Alert severity="info">A new version is available.</Alert>

examples.title: With title
examples.code:
<Alert severity="error" title="Payment failed">
  We could not charge your card. Update your billing details.
</Alert>

examples.title: Dismissible
examples.description: Pass `onClose` to render an on-brand close button.

examples.title: With an action
examples.code:
<Alert
  severity="warning"
  action={<Button variant="secondary" size="sm">Undo</Button>}
>
  Item moved to trash.
</Alert>

examples.title: Floating (toast)
examples.description: Pair `floating` with MUI's `Snackbar` to present Alert as a toast. The tinted, bordered, rounded surface reads well over arbitrary page content, so the default icon is suppressed to keep it compact.
examples.code:
<Snackbar open={open} autoHideDuration={4000} onClose={handleClose}>
  <Alert severity="success" floating onClose={handleClose}>
    Changes saved.
  </Alert>
</Snackbar>

dos: Match the `severity` to the meaning (success for confirmations, error for failures)
Keep messages short and actionable; add a `title` only when the body needs framing
Use `onClose` for dismissible, low-urgency alerts
Reserve `floating` for Alert used as a toast (e.g. inside `Snackbar`), not inline in the page
donts: Don't use an Alert to block the user — use a Dialog for responses you must collect
Don't rely on colour alone — the text must carry the meaning
Don't hardcode background, border, or text colours — the severity covers both colour schemes
Don't stack many alerts at once; surface the single most important message
accessibility: Renders with role="alert" by default; pass role="status" for lower-urgency messages
The close button and any action are keyboard-accessible and never steal focus
Icon and colour are decorative — the message text conveys the state

components.name: Avatar
components.tagline: Represents a user or entity with initials, an icon, or a photo, plus an optional status badge.

props.name: children
props.description: Initials or an icon, shown when no image `src` is provided. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL. When set, the photo fills the avatar and `children` are ignored. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: alt
props.description: Alternative text for the image, also used by screen readers. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: size
props.description: Diameter: 24px, 32px, or 40px.

props.name: shape
props.description: Corner treatment: full circle, rounded square, or square.

props.name: color
props.description: Background colour role for text / icon content. Ignored when an image renders.

props.name: badge
props.description: Shows a status dot at the bottom-right.

props.name: badgeColor
props.description: Colour of the status dot.

examples.title: Status badge
examples.description: Set `badge` to overlay a status dot at the bottom-right. The default success green conventionally reads as online / active.

examples.title: Badge colour
examples.description: There is no online / away prop — presence is conveyed by `badgeColor` alone (a convention, not an enum). Common mapping: success = online, warning = away, error = busy, neutral = offline.
examples.code:
<Avatar badge badgeColor="success">OP</Avatar>
<Avatar badge badgeColor="warning">OP</Avatar>
<Avatar badge badgeColor="error">OP</Avatar>
<Avatar badge badgeColor="neutral">OP</Avatar>

dos: Provide `alt` text whenever you set an image `src`
Use initials (one or two letters) as the fallback when no photo exists
Keep one `shape` consistent across a group of avatars
Use the `badge` dot for presence or status, not for counts
donts: Don't put more than two characters of text inside an avatar
Don't hardcode background colours — use the `color` role so both colour schemes work
Don't mix sizes within a single avatar group or stack
Don't rely on the badge colour alone to convey status — pair it with text elsewhere
accessibility: Set `alt` on image avatars so screen readers announce the person or entity
Initials and icon avatars are decorative by default — convey the name in adjacent text

components.name: Box
components.tagline: Generic, theme-aware container — a div with access to the theme through the sx prop.

props.name: sx
props.description: Styles resolved against the Neoflo theme. Numeric spacing keys (`p`, `m`, `gap`) use the spacing scale; colour strings (`bgcolor: "primary.main"`) resolve from the palette in both colour schemes.

props.name: component
props.description: Element or component rendered at the root. Polymorphic — `component="a"` also types the anchor props, so `href` is checked.

props.name: children
props.description: Box content.

props.name: ref
props.description: Forwarded to the root element.

examples.title: Basics
examples.description: Box renders a `<div>` by default. Swap in any other valid HTML tag or React component with the `component` prop.
examples.code:
<Box
  component="section"
  sx={{
    p: 2,
    borderRadius: 1,
    border: '1px dashed',
    borderColor: 'divider',
  }}
>
  This Box renders an HTML section element.
</Box>

examples.title: Customization
examples.description: Use `sx` to style any Box instance from the theme. Numbers go through the spacing scale — `p: 2` is theme spacing, not 2px — and colour strings resolve from the palette, so one snippet is correct in both colour schemes.
examples.code:
<Box
  sx={{
    width: 100,
    height: 100,
    borderRadius: 1,
    bgcolor: 'primary.main',
    '&:hover': { bgcolor: 'primary.dark' },
  }}
/>

examples.title: Flex layout
examples.description: Box is the container to reach for when a layout needs more than one axis, or uneven alignment.
examples.code:
const tile = { p: 2, borderRadius: 1, bgcolor: 'action.hover' };

<Box
  sx={{ display: 'flex', gap: 2, justifyContent: 'space-between' }}
>
  <Box sx={tile}>Left</Box>
  <Box sx={tile}>Centre</Box>
  <Box sx={tile}>Right</Box>
</Box>

examples.title: Responsive values
examples.description: Any `sx` value accepts a breakpoint object keyed by the theme breakpoints — one column on mobile, three from `md` up.
examples.code:
<Box
  sx={{
    display: 'grid',
    gap: 2,
    gridTemplateColumns: { xs: '1fr', md: 'repeat(3, 1fr)' },
  }}
>
  <Box sx={tile}>xs: 1fr</Box>
  <Box sx={tile}>md: repeat(3, 1fr)</Box>
  <Box sx={tile}>Third</Box>
</Box>

examples.title: Any element, still typed
examples.description: `component` is polymorphic: it narrows the remaining props to that element, so `href` is checked here and a typo is a build error.
examples.code:
<Box
  component="a"
  href="/tokens"
  sx={{ color: 'primary.main', fontWeight: 600 }}
>
  This Box is an anchor →
</Box>

examples.title: Reading the theme directly
examples.description: Pass a function to `sx` when a value has no shorthand — never reach for a hex. Note that an `sx` callback is a function, so it cannot cross the React Server Component boundary: use it from a `"use client"` component.
examples.code:
<Box
  sx={(theme) => ({
    pb: 1,
    borderBottom: `1px solid ${theme.palette.divider}`,
    fontFamily: theme.typography.fontFamily,
  })}
>
  Divider drawn from theme.palette.divider
</Box>

dos: Use it for layout — flex and grid containers, wrappers, and spacing between components
Set the right element with `component` so the markup stays semantic (`section`, `main`, `aside`, `ul`)
Reference the theme by name in `sx` (`bgcolor: "background.paper"`, `p: 2`) so both colour schemes and the spacing scale are handled for you
Prefer a purpose-built component when one exists — Box is the open-ended option, not the first one
donts: Don't hardcode hex, rgb, or px colour and spacing values in `sx` — use palette names and the spacing scale
Don't rebuild a component that already exists (a bordered Box is not a Card, a tinted Box is not an Alert)
Don't use the legacy system props (`<Box mt={2} />`) — MUI deprecated them in favour of `sx={{ mt: 2 }}`
Don't use `style={{}}` on a Box — it bypasses the theme and loses responsive values
accessibility: Renders a `<div>` by default, which carries no semantics — use `component` to render the element the content actually is
Box adds no ARIA of its own; when it becomes an interactive element, supply the role, focus handling, and label yourself

components.name: Button
components.tagline: Branded action button with five colour roles, three emphasis levels, and three sizes.

props.name: variant
props.description: Colour role. `secondary` renders on neutral grey surfaces; all others use their semantic colour scale.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Visual emphasis: solid fill, 1px border, or label-only.

props.name: size
props.description: Control height: 32px, 40px, or 48px.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner and disables interaction. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: startIcon / endIcon
props.description: Icon before / after the label. Use icons from @neoflo/atoms/icons.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the button and applies disabled styling.

examples.title: Primary call to action
examples.description: The main CTA on a page — one per section.

examples.title: Secondary action
examples.description: Neutral action next to a primary CTA.

examples.title: With icons
examples.code:
import { Heart, ArrowRight } from '@neoflo/atoms/icons';

<Button startIcon={<Heart />} endIcon={<ArrowRight />}>
  Save to favourites
</Button>

dos: Use `variant="primary"` for the main CTA on a page (one per section)
Use `variant="error"` for irreversible actions (delete, remove)
Use `appearance="outline"` or `appearance="text"` for secondary actions
Pair `variant="secondary"` with a primary button for cancel/back actions
donts: Don't use multiple `primary` contained buttons in the same section
Don't use `variant="error"` for cancel or dismiss actions
Don't override button colours with `sx` — pick the right variant instead
Don't use `size="sm"` for primary page-level CTAs
accessibility: Always provide visible text or aria-label for icon-only usage
Focus-visible state renders a 3px ring that meets contrast requirements

components.name: Checkbox
components.tagline: Selection control with an optional clickable label, checked, indeterminate, and disabled states.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label beside the control. When omitted, provide an `aria-label` instead.

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled checked state. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Initial state for uncontrolled usage.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires when the user toggles the control.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Mixed state for parent checkboxes over partially-selected groups. Visual only — set `checked` separately.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control and applies disabled styling.

examples.title: Disabled states
examples.code:
<Checkbox label="Unavailable" disabled />
<Checkbox label="Locked on" disabled defaultChecked />

dos: Use the `label` prop so the text is part of the click target
Provide an `aria-label` whenever there is no visible label
Use `indeterminate` on a parent checkbox over a partially-selected group
Use checkboxes for independent options — any number can be selected
donts: Don't use a Checkbox for mutually exclusive options — that's a radio group
Don't use a Checkbox to trigger an immediate action — use a Switch or Button
Don't rewrap the control in your own `FormControlLabel` — the `label` prop handles it
Don't override the checked colour — it is part of the selector identity
accessibility: The label is wired to the input via `FormControlLabel`, so clicking it toggles the control
Keyboard accessible: focusable with Tab, toggled with Space
`aria-label` is required when no visible label is rendered

components.name: Chip
components.tagline: Compact pill for tags, filters, and statuses with the same colour roles as Button.

props.name: label
props.description: Chip content. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: variant
props.description: `information`/`orange`/`purple` are only drawn at `size="sm"`; at `size="md"` they fall back to the `secondary` look.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Visual emphasis: subtle fill or 1px border. Only applies at `size="md"` — `size="sm"` always renders a flat swatch.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` = 36px pill (five roles, contained/outline, interactive). `sm` = 20px flat tag (eight roles, no states).

props.name: avatar
props.description: Leading avatar element. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: icon
props.description: Leading icon element. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: onDelete
props.description: Shows a trailing delete affordance and fires when activated. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Makes the chip clickable; hover and pressed states only render on clickable chips.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the chip and applies disabled styling.

examples.title: Flat tag colours
examples.description: `size="sm"` adds three colour roles with no pill equivalent.
examples.code:
<Chip size="sm" variant="information" label="Info" />
<Chip size="sm" variant="orange" label="Orange" />
<Chip size="sm" variant="purple" label="Purple" />

dos: Match the `variant` to the meaning (e.g. `success` for healthy states, `error` for failures)
Use `appearance="outline"` for filter chips and lower-emphasis tags
Use `onDelete` for removable selections so the affordance is consistent
Keep labels short — one or two words
donts: Don't use a Chip as a primary action — use `Button` instead
Don't rely on colour alone to communicate status — the label must carry the meaning
Don't mix sizes within one group of chips
Don't hardcode background or border colours — the variant covers both colour schemes
Don't use `information`/`orange`/`purple` at `size="md"` — they have no pill styling and fall back to `secondary`
accessibility: Clickable chips at `size="md"` are focusable and render a 3px focus-visible ring; `size="sm"` has no defined focus styling in Figma
The delete affordance is keyboard-accessible via Backspace/Delete when the chip has focus

components.name: IconButton
components.tagline: Icon-only action button with the same colour roles, emphasis levels, and sizes as Button.

props.name: variant
props.description: Colour role. `secondary` renders on neutral grey surfaces; all others use their semantic colour scale.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Visual emphasis: solid fill, 1px border, or bare glyph.

props.name: size
props.description: Square control size: 32px, 36px, or 44px.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Required for accessibility — the control has no visible text.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a spinner and disables interaction. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the button and applies disabled styling.

examples.title: Primary action
examples.code:
import { Heart } from '@neoflo/atoms/icons';

<IconButton aria-label="Save to favourites">
  <Heart />
</IconButton>

examples.title: Sizes
examples.code:
<IconButton size="sm" aria-label="Close"><X /></IconButton>
<IconButton size="md" aria-label="Close"><X /></IconButton>
<IconButton size="lg" aria-label="Close"><X /></IconButton>

dos: Always provide an `aria-label` describing the action
Use icons from `@neoflo/atoms/icons` so size and weight defaults apply
Use `appearance="text"` for toolbar and inline actions
Match the `variant` to the action semantics (e.g. `error` for delete)
donts: Don't put text inside an IconButton — use `Button` with `startIcon` instead
Don't rely on colour alone to communicate the action — the icon must be recognisable
Don't override the circular shape or fixed sizes
Don't use multiple contained `primary` icon buttons in one toolbar
accessibility: `aria-label` is required — there is no visible text fallback
Focus-visible state renders a 3px ring that meets contrast requirements

components.name: Radio
components.tagline: Single-selection control for mutually exclusive options, with an optional clickable label and a RadioGroup wrapper.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label beside the control. When omitted, provide an `aria-label` instead.

props.name: value
props.description: Value reported to the surrounding `RadioGroup` when this radio is selected.

props.name: checked
props.description: Controlled checked state. Usually managed by the surrounding `RadioGroup` instead.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Fires when the user selects the control. Usually handled on the `RadioGroup`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control and applies disabled styling.

examples.title: Radio group
examples.code:
<RadioGroup value={plan} onChange={handlePlanChange}>
  <Radio value="starter" label="Starter" />
  <Radio value="pro" label="Pro" />
  <Radio value="enterprise" label="Enterprise" />
</RadioGroup>

examples.title: Horizontal group
examples.code:
<RadioGroup row value={size} onChange={handleSizeChange}>
  <Radio value="sm" label="Small" />
  <Radio value="md" label="Medium" />
  <Radio value="lg" label="Large" />
</RadioGroup>

examples.title: Disabled options
examples.code:
<RadioGroup value={tier} onChange={handleTierChange}>
  <Radio value="free" label="Free" />
  <Radio value="paid" label="Paid" disabled />
</RadioGroup>

dos: Wrap radios in a `RadioGroup` so selection and keyboard navigation work
Use the `label` prop so the text is part of the click target
Provide an `aria-label` whenever there is no visible label
Use radios for 2–5 mutually exclusive options that should all be visible
donts: Don't use a Radio for independent options — that's a Checkbox
Don't use radios for long option lists — use a Select instead
Don't leave a radio group with no selected default unless 'none' is meaningful
Don't override the selected colour — it is part of the selector identity
accessibility: The label is wired to the input via `FormControlLabel`, so clicking it selects the control
Within a `RadioGroup`, Arrow keys move selection and Tab moves focus out of the group
`aria-label` is required when no visible label is rendered

components.name: Select
components.tagline: Dropdown field with the same static label and validation statuses as TextField, built on MUI Select.

props.name: label
props.description: Static label rendered above the field. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: children
props.description: Options, as MUI `MenuItem` elements.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: Controlled or uncontrolled selected value.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status. Colours the border and helper text; `error` also sets `aria-invalid`. Omit for the neutral state.

props.name: helperText
props.description: Supporting text below the field. Coloured by `status` when one is set.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allows selecting more than one option. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and applies disabled styling.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the field to the width of its container.

examples.title: Basic select
examples.code:
import { MenuItem } from '@mui/material';
import { Select } from '@neoflo/atoms';

<Select label="Country" defaultValue="us">
  <MenuItem value="us">United States</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem value="ca">Canada</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem value="mx">Mexico</MenuItem>
</Select>

examples.title: With helper text
examples.code:
<Select label="Role" defaultValue="editor" helperText="Controls workspace permissions">
  <MenuItem value="admin">Admin</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem value="editor">Editor</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem value="viewer">Viewer</MenuItem>
</Select>

examples.title: Validation error
examples.code:
<Select label="Plan" status="error" helperText="Choose a plan to continue">
  <MenuItem value="pro">Pro</MenuItem>
  <MenuItem value="team">Team</MenuItem>
</Select>

dos: Always provide a `label` — use `aria-label` only when a visible label is impossible
Pair every `status` with a `helperText` explaining what to fix or confirm
Use MUI `MenuItem` for options so keyboard navigation and a11y work out of the box
donts: Don't rely on border colour alone to communicate validation — set `helperText` too
Don't override the 1px border or 8px radius — they are part of the field identity
accessibility: `status="error"` sets `aria-invalid` on the field
Helper text is associated with the field via `aria-describedby`
Built on MUI `Select`, so full keyboard support (arrow keys, type-ahead, `Esc` to close) comes for free

components.name: TextField
components.tagline: Text input with a static label, validation statuses, helper text, and single or multi-line entry.

props.name: label
props.description: Static label rendered above the field. Inherited from MUI.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder shown when the field is empty.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status. Colours the border and helper text; `error` also sets `aria-invalid`. Omit for the neutral state.

props.name: helperText
props.description: Supporting text below the field. Coloured by `status` when one is set.

props.name: startAdornment
props.description: Element rendered at the start of the input, e.g. a search icon. Wrap decorative icons in MUI’s `InputAdornment` for the correct colour/spacing; interactive controls like `IconButton` can be passed directly.

props.name: endAdornment
props.description: Element rendered at the end of the input, e.g. a clear `IconButton` or a password visibility toggle.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Shows a live "length/max" counter next to the label and caps native input length. Requires `label`.

props.name: multiline
props.description: Renders a textarea instead of a single-line input.

props.name: rows
props.description: Fixes the textarea height; overflowing content scrolls (Figma inflexible / scroll variants).

props.name: minRows / maxRows
props.description: Lets the textarea grow with content between bounds (Figma flexible variant).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the field and applies disabled styling.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Stretches the field to the width of its container.

examples.title: Start icon (decorative)
examples.description: Wrap non-interactive icons in MUI’s `InputAdornment` so they pick up the correct colour and spacing.

examples.title: Clearable field (end icon button)
Start + end adornments
examples.description: Combine a decorative start icon with an interactive end icon, e.g. a password field with a show/hide toggle.

examples.title: Character counter
examples.code: <TextField label="Bio" placeholder="Tell us about yourself" maxLength={100} />

dos: Always provide a `label` — use `aria-label` only when a visible label is impossible
Pair every `status` with a `helperText` explaining what to fix or confirm
Use `minRows`/`maxRows` for free-form text so the field grows with content
Keep helper text to one short sentence
donts: Don't use placeholder text as a substitute for a label
Don't rely on border colour alone to communicate validation — set `helperText` too
Don't override the 1px border or 8px radius — they are part of the field identity
Don't use `rows` for inputs that commonly exceed the visible area unless scrolling is intended
accessibility: `status="error"` sets `aria-invalid` on the input
Helper text is associated with the input via `aria-describedby`
The static label stays visible at all times — no information is lost on focus
